workload.name: stock xv6-public forktest, 4 MiB, Bochs BIOS
workload.commandBase: XV6_LEAN=1 XV6_FIRMWARE=bochs XV6_STEPS=40000000 XV6_STOP_ON_EXPECT=1 XV6_COMMAND=$'forktest\r' XV6_EXPECT_SERIAL=$'fork test OK\n$ ' node scripts/probe-xv6-stock.mjs
workload.normalization: Remove nativeByte, nativeStats and sharedRam fields; replace rom, image and slaveImage absolute paths with <media>; retain all other report fields in original JSON order.

implementation.scope: Opt-in probe only; paged flat 32-bit CS code in plain high RAM, register MOV/CMP/TEST, memory MOV, LEA, NOP, and backward JZ/JNZ. Rechecks code bytes, cached mappings and event bounds; falls back to the JavaScript CPU at unsupported or unsafe entries.

validation: node --test test/i80386*.test.mjs: 351 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed. The full ordinary and native guest reports match after removing opt-in metadata; CPU, serial, interrupts, screen, milestones and steps are included in the comparison.
conclusion: Real-byte decode and bounded native execution work for a narrow subset without changing this xv6 guest result, but the full workload is substantially slower. No 10x gain or production readiness is claimed.
